title: Canonical isomorphisms comparing exterior presheaves and exterior sheaves
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and $n\in\mathbf N$. Let $P_n(M)$ be the sectionwise exterior-power presheaf used in $\operatorname{exteriorSheaf}(M,n)$ [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power], and let $Q_n(M)$ be the existing upstream $\operatorname{PresheafOfModules.exteriorPower}(M,n)$: both have sections $\bigwedge^n_{\mathcal O_X(U)}M(U)$ and restrictions taking wedges to wedges of restrictions. Define $\operatorname{exteriorSheafPresheafIso}(M,n):P_n(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_n(M)$ to have the identity isomorphism on every section module; naturality follows from the unique restriction maps on pure wedges. Define $\operatorname{exteriorSheafIsoExteriorPower}(M,n):\operatorname{exteriorSheaf}(M,n)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{exteriorPower}(M,n)$ to be the image of that presheaf isomorphism under the module-sheafification functor [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], where the upstream $\operatorname{exteriorPower}(M,n)$ is the sheafification of $Q_n(M)$. These are specified constructions, in every degree including zero, with no local-freeness assumption.

lean.statement:
def exteriorSheafIsoExteriorPower (M : X.Modules) (n : ℕ) :
    exteriorSheaf M n ≅ exteriorPower M n
lean.note: Reuse the two existing canonical definitions in ExteriorSheafComparison, as required by the return on 7096fcc73b37. The presheaf map is the identity on sections and the sheaf map is its sheafification.mapIso.
